title: Cursor through 2.2 can bypass the terminal allowlist through environment variables
summary: Shell built-ins can modify environment variables without allowlist approval. Prompt injection can poison variables used by trusted commands and lead to arbitrary code execution.

severity.rationale: Exploitation needs Auto-Run and Allowlist modes plus commands affected by environment variables. This is a practical precondition for unattended coding workflows.

affected.note: Vendor lists versions through 2.2 as affected.

exposure: The vendor identifies non-default Auto-Run Mode with Allowlist mode. This is not a claim that every Cursor configuration is exposed.

params.instructions: Check whether Cursor is version 2.2 or earlier and uses Auto-Run Mode together with Allowlist mode.

remediation.details: Upgrade to Cursor 2.3 or later, which improves terminal command parsing.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
